selection_basis.reason: High decision relevance with concrete main-result and ablation claims about selective memory intervention.

source.title: Remember When It Matters: Proactive Memory Agent for Long-Horizon Agents

verified_claims.claim: Terminal-Bench 2.0 Sonnet 4.5 improves 37.6%→45.9% (+8.3 pp); Opus 4.6 improves 43.5%→45.9% (+2.4 pp).
verified_claims.assessment: Verified. n=85 for each Terminal-Bench condition.

verified_claims.claim: tau2-Bench Sonnet task-weighted average improves 55.0%→61.8% (+6.8 pp); Opus improves 66.2%→68.7% (+2.5 pp).
verified_claims.assessment: Verified. Scope is the paper's airline/retail/telecom tau2-Bench evaluation.

verified_claims.claim: Full-bank passive exposure underperforms the full selective memory agent.
verified_claims.assessment: Verified under both macro and micro averages.

verified_claims.claim: An untrained Qwen3.5-27B memory agent can hurt; SFT/GRPO improve SETA reward and trained memory transfers to held-out Terminal-Bench.
verified_claims.assessment: Verified. Supports the narrower claim that memory intervention requires calibration and can be learnable; it does not establish a general deployment cost/benefit optimum.

corrections_or_clarifications.verified_scope: This is not true under every reported aggregation. Table 2: selective/full = 64.3 macro and 61.2 micro; always-inject = 63.5 macro and 61.5 micro. Selective wins the equal-domain macro average by 0.8 pp, while always-inject is 0.3 pp higher on task-weighted micro. Therefore downstream claims should say selective intervention has an advantage under the paper's macro/domain-balanced view and against passive full-bank exposure, but the evidence does not establish universal superiority to always-on injection.

Injection-only/no-bank has airline 62.0 versus baseline 68.0 (a regression) while improving retail/telecom and macro/micro overall. This supports domain-dependent harm, not a blanket claim that no-bank injection is worse overall.

Well supported by two distinct observations: passive full-bank exposure trails selective/full, and an untrained open-weight memory agent reduces SETA reward from 0.709 to 0.693. Generalize only as a mechanism hypothesis beyond these setups.

unresolved_gaps: No independent replication verified in this run.
The paper does not, in the checked evidence, report full deployment overhead in latency/token/dollar terms for the frontier memory-agent calls.
Optimal intervention frequency beyond the tested variants and >100-step persistence remain unresolved.

downstream_action.integrator: Retain the main benchmark gains, full-bank comparison, and untrained-memory negative result. Correct any statement that selective reminder/silence strictly beats always-inject across all reported averages; macro favors selective, micro slightly favors always-inject.
downstream_action.evidence_comparator: Evidence strength remains high for reported primary results, but the selective-vs-always-on conclusion must be aggregation-qualified. Independent replication remains absent.
